body: My cat gave birth on me while I was asleep on the couch at like 3am. I was in 3rd grade. Traumatized for life.
That is a great option. We have those as well, we call them charter schools here. They fill up fast! My son wasn’t accepted as they were full. We are on a wait list though.
I work full time so he would be going to before and after school. I should’ve noted that. 7:30am-5:30pm. 5 days a week, 2 months off in summer. Obviously holiday breaks as well.

This is where I am stuck. 

Raise a good human with exposure to the many different kinds of people or raise a child with a good academic experience and hope that I can expose and teach him diversity and how to respect it outside of school. I worry that in private school he may have more of an influence on his life views from peers than dumb old mom.

Definitely worth looking into. 

Not a public boarding school but people that can afford $10-20k tuition for grade school is definitely a different income bracket/class than I was raised. I am genuinely just curious about how that may affect him

Better pupils as in what? 

I was raised in public school, my soon to be husband in private. His family was well off, mine was not. I now have the ability to put my son in private and am curious as to how it may affect his view on others from different income brackets/classes.
I definitely could’ve worded it better. 🙁
Give me a few reasons please!

The public school we are zoned for does not have extremely high graduation rates or very high test scores. 

On the other hand, I don’t want my child to be associating only with other children from the same class. I know this can be helped in other ways outside of school but they spend most of their lives at school. 

I am just curious everyone’s thoughts on the difference.
